name: Egg Fried Rice
cuisine: Indo-Chinese (Mumbai street, "Chinese gaadi" and restaurant style)

ingredients.name: Basmati rice (raw), or cooked leftover rice
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅓ cup raw, or about 1⅓ cups cooked

ingredients.name: Water, for boiling the rice (only if cooking from raw)
Black pepper powder (kali mirch), or white pepper
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ tsp (a pinch in the eggs, the rest in the rice)

ingredients.name: Refined sunflower oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2½ tsp (1 tsp for the egg, 1½ tsp for the stir-fry)

ingredients.name: Spring onion (hara pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2–3 stalks; whites and greens chopped separately

ingredients.name: Salt, for the rice
ingredients.householdMeasure: a pinch (taste first; soy sauce is salty)

equipment: Wok or wide kadai (a heavy, wide frying pan also works; cook on the highest heat and don't crowd it)
Spatula (flat, or a wok ladle) and a fork for breaking up the egg and rice
Small bowl and a fork or whisk for beating the eggs
Chopping board and a sharp knife
If cooking rice from raw: a pot for boiling and draining the rice (or a pressure cooker: 1 : 1½ rice to water, 2 whistles), plus a large plate or tray to spread the rice to cool
Measuring spoons (normal teaspoons are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Rinse 65 g (⅓ cup) basmati rice in water 2–3 times until the water is nearly clear.
steps.visualCue: The water runs almost clear.
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed rice in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Hands swirling rice in cloudy water, then pouring it off.

steps.title: Boil the rice
steps.text: Boil about 700 ml water, add the rice, and cook uncovered on medium-high until just cooked but still firm.
steps.tip: Stop a minute early; soft rice turns mushy in the wok.
steps.visualCue: A grain pressed between fingers is soft outside with a tiny firm centre.
steps.cameraCheck: One grain pressed between two fingers
steps.videoShot: Rice grains rolling in boiling water.

steps.title: Drain and cool the rice
steps.text: Drain the rice, spread it on a large plate and leave it uncovered in the fridge.
steps.tip: Leftover rice from the night before is even better.
steps.visualCue: Cool to the touch, dry on the surface, grains separate.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice spread on the plate
steps.videoShot: A spatula spreading steaming rice thinly on a tray.

steps.title: Break up the rice
steps.text: Put 200 g cold cooked rice (about 1⅓ cups) in a bowl and loosen any lumps with your fingers.
steps.visualCue: Loose, separate grains, no clumps.
steps.cameraCheck: The loosened rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Fingers crumbling a lump of cold rice into grains.

steps.title: Beat the eggs
steps.text: Crack 2 eggs into a bowl, add a small pinch of salt and a pinch of pepper, and beat with a fork.
steps.visualCue: Evenly yellow, a little frothy, no streaks of white.
steps.cameraCheck: The beaten eggs in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A fork whisking eggs in a bowl.

steps.title: Chop the garlic, ginger and chilli
steps.text: Finely chop 2 garlic cloves (5 g), ½ tsp ginger (2 g) and 1 small green chilli (2 g).
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even bits.
steps.cameraCheck: The small heap on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife rocking over chopped garlic.

steps.title: Cut the spring onion
steps.text: Chop 2–3 spring onion stalks (25 g); keep the white parts and the green parts in separate heaps.
steps.visualCue: A small white heap and a larger green heap.
steps.cameraCheck: The two heaps on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing spring onion into rings.

steps.title: Dice the carrot and beans
steps.text: Peel and finely dice 25 g carrot; finely chop 20 g French beans.
steps.visualCue: Small pieces about the size of a grain of corn.
steps.cameraCheck: The diced carrot and beans
steps.videoShot: A knife dicing carrot into small cubes.

steps.title: Dice the capsicum
steps.text: Finely dice 20 g capsicum. Set out 1½ tsp soy sauce and ½ tsp vinegar near the stove.
steps.visualCue: Small green squares; sauces ready.
steps.cameraCheck: All the chopped vegetables and the sauces
steps.videoShot: An overhead shot of the prepared bowls (mise en place).

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in the wok on medium-high, pour in the eggs, let them set for 10 seconds, then stir and break them into small curds.
steps.tip: Take the eggs off while still slightly soft; they go back in later and finish cooking.
steps.visualCue: Soft, just-set yellow curds with no runny liquid, not browned.
steps.cameraCheck: The scrambled egg in the wok
steps.videoShot: A spatula pushing egg into soft folds.

steps.title: Take the eggs out
steps.text: Lift the scrambled egg onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: The wok is empty and almost clean.
steps.cameraCheck: The egg on the plate
steps.videoShot: Yellow egg curds slid onto a plate.

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Put the wok on the highest heat and add 1½ tsp oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and the first wisp of smoke appears.
steps.cameraCheck: The hot oil in the wok
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling around a hot wok.

steps.title: Fry the garlic, ginger and chilli
steps.text: Add the chopped garlic, ginger and chilli and stir.
steps.tip: Don't let the garlic brown dark; burnt garlic tastes bitter.
steps.visualCue: Sizzling, fragrant, just turning pale gold.
steps.cameraCheck: The garlic in the wok
steps.videoShot: Garlic sizzling in oil.

steps.title: Add the spring onion whites
steps.text: Add the spring onion whites and toss.
steps.visualCue: Glossy and just softened.
steps.cameraCheck: The spring onion whites in the wok
steps.videoShot: A spatula tossing white rings.

steps.title: Add carrot and beans
steps.text: Add the carrot and beans; toss on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Colours brighten; still crunchy when bitten.
steps.cameraCheck: The vegetables in the wok
steps.videoShot: Orange and green bits tossed in the wok.

steps.title: Add the capsicum
steps.text: Add the capsicum and toss.
steps.visualCue: Bright green, still crisp.
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed vegetables in the wok
steps.videoShot: Capsicum dropped onto the vegetables.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Add the loosened rice and spread it across the wok.
steps.visualCue: Rice in a thin layer touching the hot wok.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the wok
steps.videoShot: Rice tipped into the wok and spread out.

steps.title: Toss the rice
steps.text: Toss and press the rice on high heat until every grain is hot and coated in oil.
steps.tip: Spread and toss rather than stir slowly; slow stirring on low heat makes the rice sticky.
steps.visualCue: Grains look glossy and separate, and you hear a light crackle.
steps.cameraCheck: A spatula of rice lifted from the wok
steps.videoShot: Rice jumping as the wok is tossed.

steps.title: Add the sauces
steps.text: Drizzle 1½ tsp soy sauce and ½ tsp vinegar around the hot edge of the wok, then toss.
steps.visualCue: A sizzle and a toasty soy smell; the rice turns light golden-brown evenly.
steps.cameraCheck: The evenly coloured rice
steps.videoShot: Soy sauce hissing on the hot wok rim.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add the rest of the pepper, a pinch of salt only if needed after tasting, and a small pinch of sugar (optional). Toss.
steps.visualCue: Tastes savoury and lightly peppery, not too salty.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice after seasoning
steps.videoShot: Pepper dusted over the rice.

steps.title: Add back the egg
steps.text: Return the scrambled egg, break it into small pieces with the spatula and toss for 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Yellow egg flecks spread evenly through the rice.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice with egg mixed through
steps.videoShot: Egg curds folded into the rice.

steps.title: Finish with spring onion greens
steps.text: Switch off the heat, add the spring onion greens and toss once.
steps.visualCue: Bright green flecks through the rice.
steps.cameraCheck: The finished fried rice in the wok
steps.videoShot: Spring onion greens scattered over steaming rice.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a plate and serve hot.
steps.visualCue: A glossy heap of separate grains with egg, orange and green bits.
steps.cameraCheck: The served plate
steps.videoShot: Rice spooned into a mound on a plate.

reasons: stir-fried, not deep-fried, with a measured 2½ tsp of mostly unsaturated oil; 2 eggs give about 20 g good-quality protein, B12, vitamin D and selenium, and the vegetables add vitamin A, C and K. Against it: white basmati rice digests fast (high glycaemic load), fibre is only about 4 g, cholesterol is high (about 370 mg from 2 yolks) and soy sauce brings about 900 mg sodium. Restaurant plates use much more oil, soy sauce and often MSG, fewer vegetables and a bigger rice portion, and usually come with fried Manchurian.

researchRating.basis: one of the most loved and most-cooked Indo-Chinese dishes in India, with recipes on every major Indian recipe site (Swasthi's Recipes, Ranveer Brar, Sanjeev Kapoor, Yummy Tummy Aarthi, My Food Story, Raksha's Kitchen, Vismai Food) and listed by almost every Indo-Chinese and Mughlai outlet on the delivery apps; widely praised as quick, cheap and a good use of leftover rice. Small deduction because restaurant versions are often called oily or bland, and it is seen as a simple everyday dish rather than a treat.

storage: Cool and refrigerate within 1 hour (cooked rice can grow Bacillus cereus if left warm). Fridge: up to 1 day, at most 2, in an airtight box. Freezer: possible for up to 1 month in a flat bag, but the egg turns rubbery; fridge is better. To reheat, sprinkle 1 tbsp water and toss in a hot pan for 2–3 min, or microwave covered for 1½–2 min, stirring halfway, until steaming hot throughout. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Egg fried rice omelette (Omurice-style, as in Ranveer Brar's Egg Fried Rice Manchurian). Beat 1 egg with a pinch of salt, cook it as a thin omelette in a non-stick pan, place a heap of reheated fried rice on one half, fold it over and serve with a spoon of chilli sauce or Manchurian gravy. The fresh egg wrap makes day-old rice feel like a new restaurant dish.
burnOff: about 7.6 km of running (530 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.6 km of brisk walking (about 2 h 10 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With a side of Manchurian gravy (about +225 kcal), add about 3.2 km of running.

navratri.reason: egg, rice, garlic, spring onion and table salt are all avoided on the common North and West Indian vrat rule set

ekadashi.reason: rice is the grain most strictly avoided on Ekadashi, and egg is also avoided

jain.reason: egg is not allowed in Jain food; garlic, ginger, carrot and spring onion are also excluded

ramadan.reason: no meat, so there is no halal concern; a filling, high-protein plate for iftar or sehri, but keep the soy sauce to 1 tsp for sehri because salt drives thirst during the fast

jain.reason: contains egg, which Jain food does not allow, plus garlic, ginger, carrot and spring onion (roots and bulbs); for Jain, use the Jain Vegetable Fried Rice variant of dish 43

vegan.reason: contains egg; see the Vegan variant (tofu fried rice)

pescatarian.reason: no meat, poultry or fish; eggs are normally part of a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: egg is not a sattvik food, and the dish also has garlic and spring onion; dropping garlic and onion does not make it sattvik

glutenFree.reason: ordinary soy sauce sold in India is brewed with wheat; use a gluten-free tamari. No hing is used

dairyFree.reason: no milk, curd, butter, ghee, cream or paneer

variants.reason: egg defines this dish and Jain food does not allow egg; for a Jain plate use the Jain Vegetable Fried Rice variant of Chicken Fried Rice (dish 43).
